title: Methane (CH₄) — Carbon Tetravalency
description: Explore the foundational building block of organic chemistry with perfect tetrahedral symmetry.

steps.prompt: Carbon has 4 valence electrons and forms 4 single covalent bonds with hydrogen. In 3D space, what angle keeps all 4 bonds furthest apart?
steps.explanation: Excellent! In three-dimensional space, four equidistant charge clouds point toward the corners of a regular tetrahedron with 109.5° angles.

steps.prompt: Rotate methane in 3D using your hand or mouse to see that no matter how you turn it, every H-C-H angle is identical.
steps.explanation: Because all four bonds are identical and there are no lone pairs, methane exhibits perfect Sp3 tetrahedral symmetry.

steps.prompt: What is the valency of carbon in all saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes)?
steps.explanation: Carbon is tetravalent (valency = 4), which allows it to form vast chains and rings of organic compounds through catenation.
